02 / Context

Product goal

From reports to verified fixes

Help enterprise teams complete verified SEO fixes.

Liferay DXP helps enterprises manage websites and portals. Its existing SEO capabilities were spread across page editing and content management.

  • Product goal. Bring issue discovery, prioritization, and remediation into one workflow.
  • My ownership. Led SEO Studio’s product experience, from problem analysis and experience architecture to core workflows, AI interaction, and validation planning.
  • Case study focus. AI Fix, the decision-intensive part of that larger product.

03 / Research

End-to-end journey

Three stages of the task

Map the full task before focusing on Review & Apply.

Research completed

  • Interviewed the liferay.com Marketing team and our SEO Expert about real SEO work.
  • Used liferay.com as a concrete case to map the target persona and end-to-end user journey.
Discover & PrioritizeWhich issue should I fix first?Review & ApplyWhat am I approving?Verify & ContinueIs the issue resolved?
  • Discover & Prioritize. Help users identify issues worth acting on.
  • Review & Apply. Understand the proposal before authorizing a change to live website content.
  • Verify & Continue. Confirm resolution, recover from failure, and move to the next issue.

Review & Apply became the focus because this is where a suggestion becomes a decision to change real content. Persona and journey exports are pending.

04 / Challenge

Decision barriers

Transparency / control / outcome

How might we help users make informed, confident decisions about AI-generated SEO fixes?

From “AI trust” to specific decision barriers

  • Held a workshop with the PM and SEO Expert, using the journey to examine user concerns.
  • Reviewed Gemini and Claude for ways to explain generated content and retain control before execution.
  1. 01

    Lack of transparency

    Users may see the output without understanding why it addresses the SEO issue.

  2. 02

    Limited control

    Users may be unsure about affected pages, editing, or recovery after applying a fix.

  3. 03

    Unclear outcome

    Users may see “applied” without knowing whether the SEO issue was resolved.

Working hypotheses from the workshop and comparative research. They still need validation with users.

05 / Solution

Three design strategies

Understand / control / verify

Design for understanding, approval, and verified resolution.

01

Make the AI proposal understandable.

Design strategy · Validation pending

  • Start with the current SEO issue and why it needs attention.
  • Compare Current and Proposed content so users can inspect the differences.
  • Explain the rationale and expected improvement in plain language, with effectiveness checked after Apply.

What to validate. Can users explain the reason for the change and identify the differences in their own words?

02

Give users control before they approve a change.

Design strategy · Validation pending

  • Preview the target page and affected scope before Apply.
  • Allow editing before approval and provide a recovery path.
  • Use confirmation appropriate to the risk and breadth of the change.

Design tradeoff. “AI proposes, user approves.” Assess informed approval alongside edits, abandonment, and reversions, rather than optimizing Apply Rate alone. Actual Preview / Edit / Apply / Revert scope is pending.

03

Verify the SEO issue after the change is applied.

Design strategy · Validation pending

  • Show execution status and rerun relevant SEO checks where supported.
  • When validation passes, show what was resolved and offer the next issue.
  • When validation fails, explain the current state, failure reason, and available next action.

Supporting comparison · already built in the page

Execution success
The change was saved.
Issue resolution
Relevant checks confirm the issue is resolved.

Success criterion. Count an AI Fix as complete when the change is applied and the relevant issue validation passes. Passing an SEO check does not establish a search-ranking improvement.

These strategies connect the Review & Apply decision to the complete optimization task. Screens, implementation scope, and validation evidence remain to be added.

06 / Validation

Test the decision

Comprehension / control / resolution

Validate what users understand, approve, and verify.

Planned validation

  • Understanding. Can users explain the recommendation and identify Current / Proposed differences?
  • Control. Do users understand the scope, adjust content when needed, and make an informed Apply decision?
  • Outcome. Can users distinguish a saved change from a resolved issue and choose the next action?
